 Victoria and Melbourne Stars wicketkeeper Sam Harper will play in the first T20I against England on Saturday night

 Sam Harper slamming sixes is must-watch 
 Sam Harper will become the first Victorian to debut at the MCG since Scott Boland, with the wicketkeeper a confirmed starter for Australia in the series-opening T20I against England.
 National selector Tony Dodemaide revealed Harper would play in Saturday's first T20 prior to the keeper's own press conference on Friday afternoon. 
 Harper gets his opportunity with first-choice gloveman Josh Inglis to sit out the five-game series to prepare for the Test summer against New Zealand.
 Whereas Boland had played one-day internationals five years prior to his epic 6-7 on Test debut in the 2021 Boxing Day Ashes Test, this will be Harper's maiden appearance in Australian colours.
 "It's especially cool as a Victorian to be able to play your debut at the MCG, so very excited," Harper told reporters on match eve.

 -->
 Harper stoked ahead of 'especially cool' MCG debut 
 The 29-year-old's rise with the bat in the past two summers has been immense, going from out of Victoria's Sheffield Shield side at the end of the 2024-25 season to Test and T20I squad call-ups 18 months later.
 "A few years ago, I just made a promise to myself that however long; whether it be one more BBL at the time, two more BBLs, cricket in Belgium or cricket in Sri Lanka, wherever I went, I was going to be me and I was going to put my best foot forward and enjoy it and start playing like I would have as an under-11," Harper added.
 "Belgium, Sri Lanka or wherever the past 12 to 18 months has taken me, right through to South Africa (with the Test squad), I feel like I've just played with a smile on my face and actually let what I know I can do come out, instead of hindering myself by putting too much pressure on myself."
 Harper is the reigning BBL player of the tournament following a career-best campaign last summer (381 runs at an average of 54), with the allrounder also dominating in the Lankan Premier League with 425 runs for champions Galle Gallants.
 Finch backs 'ultra damaging' former teammate for Australia debut 
 After scoring a century on Australia A debut, he then earned a call-up to the Test squad for last month's South Africa tour, again with Inglis missing through injury.
 Travis Head, Matthew Renshaw, Cameron Green (now in concussion protocols) and Cooper Connolly join Inglis in turning their attention to the four Tests against New Zealand following Australia ODI series loss, with Connolly and Inglis set to play for WA in next week's Sheffield Shield match against Tasmania at Perth Stadium.
 Shield showdown looms as Test squad delayed 
 Dodemaide didn't reveal any other pieces of Australia's XI for the series opener and neither did England skipper Harry Brook, whose side is red hot in the T20 format having risen to No.1 in the world with seven straight wins over India and Sri Lanka during their home summer.
 Like Australia, England have a number of fresh faces in their T20 squad due to their own Test tour of South Africa right after the series.
 Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker have all been rested following the ODIs, with Brook and wicketkeeper Jordan Cox to depart for South Africa following the fourth T20 in Sydney.
 "We're on a really good run in T20s now, we're playing really good cricket and it's more of that really," Brook said.
 "We've come out here to try and win the series; we're trying to pick the best XI and there will be some opportunities for guys that haven't played before.
 "We've got an 18-year-old (Thomas Rew) in the squad, a couple of young bowlers as well (Eddie Jack and Henry Crocombe), which is really exciting for English cricket to be able to get those lads the opportunity to be in and around an England squad."
